chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mirdas from Sa'dan ibn Muslim from one of our companions who said:

Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) went out for one of his needs, so he passed by a man being penalized during the winter. So he said: 'Glory be to Allah! This is not befitting!' So I said, 'And for this is a Penalty (Hadd)?' He said: 'It befits the man applying the Penalty during the winter that he applies it during the heat of the day, and for the one who applies a Penalty during the summer, is that he should apply it during the coldness of the day'.

key_terms.يُحَدُّ: Being subjected to a Hadd (fixed legal penalty)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the timing of applying Hadd penalties in relation to seasons and temperature?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the principle of *mu'asarah* (conforming to the season) in applying Hadd penalties, ensuring that the physical burden of the punishment is proportionate to the environmental conditions. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on justice (*'adl*) and mercy (*rahmah*), where the harshness of the penalty is balanced against the natural elements to prevent undue suffering. This specific ruling highlights the dynamic nature of Islamic law, adapting fixed penalties to temporal contexts to maintain their intended corrective purpose.
